body.text: Research start: 2026-11-03T06:26:10Z (date -u). Hard deadline 2026-11-03T14:26:10Z. Reconstruct the video and validate or document an exception within the Stage 1 60-minute budget before recording criteria and building the training simulation. Task: white then black charger, each picked up from right, reoriented with blades up, carried left and released upright; use observed wrist pose as reference. All success claims will be my own simulation criteria and evidence.

Reference reconstruction in progress (start 06:26:10Z; Stage 1 deadline 07:26:10Z). Scene decomposition written after inspection of sampled and event frames. SAM3 segmentation and HaWoR initialization completed. Raw object trackers: median IoU white 0.924, black 0.868, but black blade-axis ambiguity after turning and camera drift made raw 3D motion physically inconsistent. Rejected accumulated background rotation (18 degrees drift) and ill-conditioned homography translation (>1 m). Retain fixed gravity-normal rotation prior, infer smoothed camera translation from passive plugs, and enforce a shared tabletop for observed side/upright rest phases. Constrained silhouette IoU approximately 0.852 white, 0.860 black; hidden turn frames explicitly invalid. Preliminary 2-second MuJoCo rest check drift <0.04 mm. Provided unchanged MANO fitting now runs against this scene. Main remaining reconstruction risks: precise depth, hidden grasp contacts, intersection and hand scale.

The unchanged MANO fitter has only nearest-hand-point contact, so it can satisfy contact by a middle finger while the thumb floats 65–90 mm away. It also has no finger self-collision loss. A contact-weight refit restores proximity but still fails self-intersection (20.2% of valid frames). Testing an explicitly documented local copy with an opposing thumb/distal-finger term and distal capsule separation; installed code remains unchanged. Format checker reports VALID with absolute paths, but the current geometric validation fails self-intersection; I will not call that a valid reconstruction. Stage 1 time remaining approximately 35 minutes.

Reconstruction elapsed ~31 minutes. Explicit thumb/finger contact in a local fitter copy passes anatomical-contact validation (opposed grasp fraction 0.867 white, 1.0 black) and proximity (median minimum distance 2.35/0.73 mm). It still fails self-intersection, mainly middle/ring in approach/withdrawal. Testing larger distal capsule margins and stronger silhouette fitting; separate floating-scale experiment tests the fixed-scale assumption. Known limits: white object is heavily occluded, many hand frames fail mask IoU after enforcing contact, and inferred depth needs a 25 mm uncertainty. Verification draft is written from demonstration measurements but no policy has been judged or simulation built.

body.text: Reference version 1 recorded as r0005 at 07:02:23Z, before any training-simulation construction, and within 37 minutes of research start. The format checker is VALID and original geometric validation overall PASS with retained warnings. Criteria v1 defines ordered white/black physical pickup, ~0.25 m left transfer, upright unsupported settling, wrist similarity, hardware compliance and ten held-out complete episodes. Next: build the public right-hand model and controllers in MuJoCo, retarget the recorded wrist/objects, diagnose a physical contact baseline, then train a deployable closed-loop PPO network and report its baseline ablation.

Robot replay exposed an untested limitation of reconstruction v1: some inferred/fitted human wrist and hand geometry falls below the tabletop, although the provided validator reports PASS because its physics check tests objects, not hand-table intersection. Do not treat validator PASS as evidence for this missing check. The compiled right hand mass is exactly 0.6878 kg and a 2 s impedance/PD hold has zero hardware violations. Before learning, add an explicit hand-table constraint in a local fitter copy, measure penetration of every hand vertex against the tabletop, and record a corrected reference if it improves within the 60-minute reconstruction budget (deadline 07:26:10Z).

body.text: Simulation v1 r0012 recorded after reconstruction v2 and criteria v2. Correctly randomized reference baseline: 0/10 successes, all ten wrist/hardware checks pass, neither plug picked up. A direct human finger retarget crossed middle/ring tips and caused release back-drive; base abduction and unused support fingers were simplified rather than weakening physics/limits. Reset semantics were checked and corrected before recording the simulation. PPO run ppo01 now trains a deployable 136-input/26-residual actor with explicit finger-contact proximity, object-position and blade-axis rewards, and pre-grasp curricula followed by the full sequence. Reference/base performance remains separately reported; no scripted solution is claimed.

PPO01 training curves show very few opposed contacts and no lift bonus yet; this is not a verification result. While the fixed run completes, study static grasp reachability offline with constrained least-squares IK for thumb plus index/middle pads, preserving the recorded wrist neighborhood and hardware limits. Such optimization is analysis/reference construction only, never execution-time planning or an alternative RL algorithm. The original reference baseline remains 0/10; if a revised base is used later, evaluate and report it separately.

body.text: PPO03 checkpoint2174976 samples is FAIL0/10; white pickup2/10,black0/10,wrist8/10,hardware10/10. Stopped the run at2549760 samples rather than spending the remaining budget on the weak guide. Offline contact studies show reversed white Z-contact ordering plus extra4mm bounded position-target grip compression reaches16.8deg white/29.9deg black and transfers both left with zero hardware violations nominally, but both still topple at release. End-face pinches and small phase-feedback lookahead were rejected after native-physics tests. Next improve timed lowering/release and use this stronger guide for PPO; no numerical criteria or original wrist reference changes.

Next actor features add deterministic forward kinematics of noisy encoders and the observed wrist, using only constant public robot geometry: three fingertip positions/normals in the observed active-object frame, plus current constant base wrist target. These are derived from permitted proprioception/object states; they do not read true simulation link poses, contacts, forces or physical parameters. Scratch kinematics receives noisy q and observed wrist only. This keeps policy_observations deployable. Residual decisions are filtered0.75 previous+0.25new to reduce target jitter; controllers/hardware limits unchanged. Fresh PPO initialization will avoid carrying the regressed PPO03 grip biases.

mapping.method: Fixed MANO-root to anatomical-palm rotation, least-squares rotational mean across valid hand frames. Robot +Y palm normal, -Z middle MCP direction. Mount translation aligns palm frames plus one constant local morphology offset, justified by 20--30 mm shorter robot reach and 10.5 mm initial replay table penetration; invalid gaps linearly/Slerp interpolated and labelled inferred.

fingers.method: Offline bounded nonlinear least squares with exact MuJoCo site Jacobians. During grasps, match thumb and nearby opposing finger MANO surface contacts projected onto the plug body to pad surfaces, nominal 0.3 mm compression; otherwise match tips. Long-finger base abduction held at zero and ring/little gently open because direct human retargeting crossed middle/ring tips and produced back-drive speed violations. Final errors measured after these choices, 3-frame smoothing and 20%-speed target limiting. Used only as reference/base, not runtime trajectory optimization.

Native objects remain free and the base fails complete task. Original reference.npz remains unchanged for wrist verification.

body.text: Simulation v4 has been recorded. Correction to its baseline prose: the actual per-criterion counts and supplied metrics are white pickup9/10, black10/10, wrist10/10, hardware10/10, complete0/10; the phrase both pickups10/10 was a summary typo. PPO04 uses a fresh179-input network, small initial Gaussian logstd=-2.5,26independent residuals smoothed0.75previous+0.25new,48environments and6M planned samples. It keeps the PPO03 task-heavy rewards, improves index proximity shaping, and removes constant already-placed-white reward from synthetic black-only curriculum resets. Hypothesis: the more capable guide and noisy-proprioception FK features make fine roll/release corrections learnable without the earlier pickup regression.

The six-action alternative is a residual PPO over a reference controller, permitted by LEARNING.md. At execution it uses only table interpolation, arithmetic of permitted object/wrist state, bounded target offsets and a release latch derived from object tilt/bottom/transfer. No IK, search, rollout simulation or trajectory optimization runs online. PPO chooses finger-turn lead30–90deg (zero-action60), extra grip compression1–7mm, wrist gap-axis roll+-0.30rad, XY offsets+-15mm and release-tilt threshold5–25deg. The wrist time guide is retained, and opening is shifted to the observed release location. Zero-action nominal test still fails both final placements; hardware passes and wrist RMS40.64mm narrowly fails40mm. This controller is an unsolved baseline, not the learned solution.

body.text: Simulationv5 baseline holds white upright6/10 and black0/10; complete0/10, hardware10/10, wrist3/10 (position RMS37.54–40.68mm). It should learn phase lead/grip strength and a brief wrist roll to finish black rotation, then a safer release threshold/location. PPO04 continues independently with26residuals in simv4. Both algorithms are PPO; all evaluated checkpoints will receive curves,3-viewvideos,iteration andverification records.

PPO04 completed both pickups/placements and all wrist/hardware/final-hold checks in10/10; legacy evaluator reports8/10 because white_preserved starts at the FIRST0.1s table-rest interval. In seed1001 the extra tilt reaches80.06deg at5.26s, seed1008 reaches15.94deg at5.92s, both before black phase8.667s; maximum white tilt during black is0deg (numerical~1e-6). Visual inspection shows further white manipulation/recovery before final release, not a completed-white stage followed by black. body.text: Final reflection at 2026-11-03T11:00:14.881314+00:00, elapsed4.568h from start06:26:10Z, before14:26:10Z hardlimit. Stopping because own verification r0038 is PASS10/10 under recordedcriteriav2; nominal1/1, zero-actionbase0/10. Selected fresh residualPPO04 trained6008832samples in1915s,48environments,179deployableinputs/26filteredtargetresiduals. Referencev2 remained fixed after55m53s Stage1. What worked: native spec-faithful wrist/fingercontrollers, corrected reconstruction hand-table geometry, deeper/reordered pad-contactguide, index posture exploration, noisy-encoderFKfeatures and stronger task rewards. What failed: direct human-tip replay, two-point roll guide, early independentcurl and lower-dimensional phase/Cartesian-feedback alternatives. Final measurement correction: original8/10 evaluator counted continued white manipulation as failure of preservation duringblack. Corrected fixedwindow8.667–16s and actualfinalwhitecompletionbeforeblack yield10/10 with bit-identical trajectories; an additional stricter post-final-release audit also passes all10. Seed1001 has a visible recovery beforeblack, seed1008 a smaller preblack transient; neither is hidden. All16000nativehardwareticks pertrial pass; wristRMS34.49–34.68mm/13.93–13.99deg. PPO05 completed inparallel but was not held-out evaluated or selected; its artifacts remain. Analysis-only late-turn/contact variants were discarded, not used for final policy. Limits: narrow ten-seed simulation perturbations, rigid convex/box contacts and inferred friction/inertia/monocular depth. Next research would test broader perturbations, calibrate pad compliance/contact material and independently assess real-hand transfer; no such transfer is claimed.
